messages:
Ravi Sundaram: Quick postmortem question — we have a parity gap between Java and Kotlin SDKs around 401+retry semantics. Java sample retries fine, Kotlin sample returns EOF and logs 'retry suppressed'. Anyone seen this combo (streaming body + auth refresh)?
Elena Voss: yup, seen it. Which retry implementation are you using in each sample? Java often uses a custom Call wrapper in sample guide, Kotlin uses pure Interceptor.
Ravi Sundaram: exactly. Java sample wraps the Call and clones before executing, Kotlin sample has a RetryInterceptor that does chain.proceed(newRequest). Logs show connection closed during write then okhttp suppresses retry due to non-repeatable body.
Chris Wang: that matches okhttp behavior. chain.proceed() consumes RequestBody once. If the body is streaming (one-shot) it's gone. A clone of Call rebuilds the request+body path. Interceptor API doesn't expose Call.clone().
Ravi Sundaram: got it. We should not expect parity unless we change Kotlin sample. Proposal: change Kotlin sample to either (A) buffer small payloads into repeatable bodies, or (B) promote a Call-wrapper approach in docs showing how to do retries outside interceptors. Thoughts?
Elena Voss: prefer (A) for quickstart: transparent BufferingRequestBody for <=64KB, with opt-in config. For advanced users, show (B) as pattern. Also add a clear error when retry suppressed.
Chris Wang: +1. Also add test coverage: MockWebServer with SocketPolicy.DISCONNECT_DURING_REQUEST_BODY to ensure buffered path succeeds and non-buffered path emits a clear NonRepeatableRequestBody log.
Ravi Sundaram: here's the RetryInterceptor snippet currently in Kotlin sample:
```
class RetryOnAuthInterceptor : Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val req = chain.request()
    val resp = chain.proceed(req)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      Auth.refreshBlocking()
      val newReq = req.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${Auth.token}")
        .build()
      return chain.proceed(newReq)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```
Elena Voss: that's the anti-pattern. chain.proceed(req) already sent the body. For retry you need a fresh call. In samples we can: 1) check if req.body?.isOneShot == true then fail fast with guidance; 2) otherwise proceed and handle retry. Note: RequestBody doesn't have isOneShot API; you'd need to detect common streaming types or track content length unknown / chunked.
Chris Wang: you can heuristically detect if body is instance of okhttp3.RequestBody created from BufferedSource vs known repeatable implementations. Another pragmatic approach: attempt to buffer up to a limit: copy body to Buffer and use a new RequestBody from that buffer for replay.
Ravi Sundaram: good. For the sample I'm going to implement buffer-if-small. I'll add a helper: fun maybeBuffer(request: Request, maxBuffer: Long): Request { if (body.size <= maxBuffer) replaceWithBuffered() } and we'll document behavior/opt-in.
Elena Voss: also update quickstart: explain why preemptive refresh is sometimes preferred: if token TTL is short, refresh before writing body to avoid mid-flight 401s. Provide example hook in AuthManager.
Ravi Sundaram: noted. Also a subtle mobile issue: callTimeout vs socketTimeout. If auth.refresh blocks the write for longer than callTimeout, the call will error before retry logic runs. We should recommend increasing callTimeout for mobile quickstart or performing refresh off-path.
Chris Wang: yes — include example showing OkHttp client config: callTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS) for mobile or handle pre-flight auth.
bot-ci: created ticket RD-INF-9123: "sdk: kotlin/java parity - non-repeatable request body causes suppressed retry; add buffered-retry opt-in, docs, and tests" and attached logs.
Ravi Sundaram: I'll send a small PR to kotlin-samples to buffer <=64KB and add a clear log: "Retry suppressed: request body is not repeatable. See docs: <link>". Also will add a unit test using MockWebServer DISCONNECT_DURING_REQUEST_BODY.
Elena Voss: add telemetry event when retry suppressed to measure customer impact. Use event key: sdk.retry_suppressed_non_repeatable. Include payload_size and platform.
Chris Wang: agree. One more suggestion: make buffering opt-in and default to off to avoid surprising memory usage. Quickstart should present recommended opt-in configuration.
Ravi Sundaram: will do opt-in. PR will include sample snippet and docs blurb. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
